title: Build Prayer Gradually Without Shame
whyMatters: Prayer is central to Muslim life, but learning it can be hard at first. A gentle on-ramp helps you keep moving without turning every mistake into a reason to quit.

exactActions.text: Learn the shape before the details
subSteps: Learn the five names and times of prayer.
Watch or read a simple guide to the basic movements.
Keep a short reference nearby while practicing.
Choose one prayer you are most likely to catch daily.
Build consistency there before adding more.
If you miss it, restart at the next prayer without spiraling.

exactActions.text: Use what you know while learning Arabic
subSteps: Begin memorizing Al-Fatiha in small pieces.
Read from a paper or phone while learning if needed.
Ask a teacher what minimum beginner recitation to use in your situation.
Do not measure your faith by perfection.
Notice that every attempt builds familiarity.
Ask Allah to make prayer beloved and steady for you.

obstacles.solution: Missing prayers while learning is common. Use reminders, start with an anchor prayer, and ask a qualified teacher how to make up missed prayers in your situation.
Learning in private is fine. Allah sees your effort, and every Muslim had to learn the movements and words at some point.

tinyVersion: Choose one prayer to protect today, even if you need a guide beside you.
unlocksNext: Once you have an on-ramp, the full prayer step feels less like a wall and more like a path.

commonQuestions.problem: Can I pray while reading from a guide?
commonQuestions.solution: Many beginners use a written guide while learning. Ask a local teacher for details, especially once you are ready to refine your prayer.

contextNotes.title: At work or school
contextNotes.body: Start by identifying quiet spaces and realistic prayer windows. If accommodation is needed, speak calmly and keep the request practical.
